coverage.main: Read all nine pages of arXiv 2109.04176v3 (2 January 2022, AAAI 2022 copyright): Introduction with Figures 1-2, method, Algorithm 1, Experiments with Tables 1-4, Figures 3-4 and references.
coverage.supplement: No appendix or supplement is included or referenced. The AAAI proceedings PDF was not retrieved separately.
coverage.excluded_results: Figure 3 is qualitative. White-box success on the surrogate ViTs is not reported. The later IEEE TIP extension cited in the repository README is a different publication and is not reviewed here.

result_groups.population: One ImageNet validation image per class, 'correctly classified by all models'; ViT-B/16, PiT-B, CaiT-S-24, Visformer-S surrogates; eight ViT victims (the other models)
result_groups.outcome: MASR: mean over surrogates of ASR, where ASR is 'the proportion of generated adversarial examples from the surrogate model that are successfully misclassified by the black-box victim model'
result_groups.evidence: The sample is explicitly restricted to images every model classifies correctly. ASR is defined over the generated adversarial examples, with no source-success filter.

result_groups.population: Same image set; four normally trained and three ensemble-adversarially trained CNN victims
result_groups.evidence: Same explicit sample and ASR definition.

result_groups.population: Same image set; ViT-B/16 surrogate; victims grouped as ViTs, normal CNNs, robust CNNs
result_groups.outcome: average ASR over victims of each type
result_groups.evidence: Same explicit sample and ASR definition.

result_groups.locator: Introduction Figures 1(b), 2; Ablation Studies Table 4, Figure 4 (p. 7)
result_groups.population: 2,000 randomly sampled ImageNet validation images; ViT-B/16 surrogate; black-box ViTs and CNNs
result_groups.evidence: The ablation sample is described as random; a clean-correct filter is not stated. The general ASR definition applies.

f1.evidence: No clean accuracy is reported for any model.

f2.evidence: The three main scopes are explicitly clean-correct for every model (yes); the 2,000-image ablations are unresolved. Positive conditioning evidence.

f3.evidence: ASR is defined as the proportion of generated adversarial examples misclassified by the victim, without selection by surrogate success.

f4.evidence: Every reported value averages ASRs over surrogates or victims; the number of images (one per class) is not stated as a count.

f5.evidence: L-infinity epsilon = 16 with 10 iterations for all results.

f6.evidence: The official repository provides the sampled clean images (clean_resized_images.zip), attack code and an evaluator on timm models, which could support recomputation. The archive contents, the models' correspondence to 2021 timm weights, and execution were not verified.

artifact_checks.result: Linked in the paper. Listed via the GitHub API (29 files, head 3 July 2024; README also cites a 2023 TIP extension): clean_resized_images.zip, our_attacks.py, our_method.py, evaluate.py, model.py, dataset.py, image_name_to_class_id_and_name.json. evaluate.py records top-1 prediction and ground truth for every adversarial image in a folder; artifact evidence only. Archive not downloaded; not executed.

bounds_checks.reason: Rates are over images all models classify correctly and are averaged over surrogates, so no unconditional matched bound applies.
No clean accuracy on the 2,000-image sample.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. Field 3 'no' relies on the ASR definition as a proportion of generated adversarial examples; an independent recoder applying a stricter wording test could code unclear.
